title: Non-Gaussian Inference for AIPW under Adaptive Designs with a Critically Rare Arm
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; field lift requires a new kernel or application, not a bounded repair.
gap_reasons: The delivered core is a uniform finite-transfer and atom-safe coverage theorem for a tightly structured deterministic-profile subclass, not inference over general rare-arm adaptive experiments.

The exact diameter frontiers are proved and attained only within selected two-sign late-void experiments; on Li and Zhao's broader class only the converses transfer, with no globally matching confidence procedure.
The exhaustive certificate is justified through a net, truncation, and convolution construction but has neither a complexity guarantee nor an end-to-end implementation.
Publication cleanup: replace the generalized-Dickman Poisson representation's Bhattacharjee--Goldstein 2019 attribution with the attested Bhattacharjee--Molchanov 2020 source.
Publication cleanup: position Barbour--Utev 1999 substantively against the finite stopped signed-mark transfer, or remove it.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a computable finite adaptive-to-signed-compound-Poisson transfer, atom-safe coverage with oracle slack, and exact pairwise late-void frontiers, including clipped residual and intensity optimization. The field claim collapsed because the positive procedure still assumes an every-n structured profile and early-QV contract, while matching attainment is pair-specific and the practical certificate lacks polynomial complexity or an end-to-end implementation. A field re-raise needs a new larger-class kernel or a genuine consumer bridge, not another bounded revision of this note.
tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's original structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the retained constant-intensity clipped-ramp theorem optimizes the residual late-void obstruction under honesty for the selected pair; its eventual profile exactness is not an unconditional structured-class converse. A distinct pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) yields the jointly optimized pair-honesty envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\), with residual and intensity elbows that may occur in either order. Direct every-\(n\) inclusion transfers the converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. Exact attainment is pairwise only. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\), directed \(13/32\), and high-hazard \(0.442M\) results remain unchanged.
gap: Li and Zhao establish design-based Gaussian AIPW inference under variance-convergence and Lindeberg conditions, and Waudby-Smith et al. establish generic anytime-valid martingale intervals under predictable logging. Neither result calibrates the discontinuous signed compound-Poisson law that remains when rare-arm cumulative hazard is bounded, nor does either derive an all-confidence-set width obstruction from the complete logged experiment.
fill: The project supplies a computable adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer, a simultaneous profile enclosure and directed convolution certificate, an explicit directed-dyadic bandwidth with a vanishing radius charge, an atom-safe coverage and oracle-radius theorem, and a separate void-event lower bound for arbitrary confidence sets.
